artists.biography:
Isobel Campbell (born on 27 April 1976) is a Scottish singer, cellist and composer in the indie and rock genres. She was born in Glasgow. She is a former member of the Scottish indie pop band Belle & Sebastian, but left the group to pursue a solo career, first as The Gentle Waves, and later under her own name. Recently, she has collaborated with singer Mark Lanegan on three albums.
Isobel Campbell's music has been described as either indie pop, chamber pop or singer-songwriter. Regardless of genre, Campbell makes gentle and sombre music, often using classical instruments and her bright, slightly nasal voice with bittersweet and ironic songwriting.

perplexity.description:
There Is No Other... marks Isobel Campbell's return to solo recording after years away from the studio. Released in February 2020 on Cooking Vinyl, the album showcases Campbell's evolution as a songwriter and performer, moving beyond the delicate indie pop sensibilities that defined her work with Belle & Sebastian and her collaborative projects with Mark Lanegan. The record demonstrates considerable stylistic range, blending folk, pop, and world music influences with varied instrumentation including acoustic guitar, bossa nova rhythms, Asian-influenced strings, and banjo, creating what one reviewer described as having "more colours and textures" than typical singer-songwriter fare.

Campbell's distinctive vocal approach—often described as diaphanous and gentle—remains central to the album's identity, though she proves her versatility by shifting between intimate, whispered passages and more forceful, expressive delivery. The tracklist includes a cover of Tom Petty's "Running Down a Dream" alongside original compositions that address both personal and environmental themes, with songs like "The Heart of It All" incorporating social commentary. The album's production values and compositional ambition reflect Campbell's maturity as an artist, with each track maintaining its own distinct character rather than adhering to a uniform sonic palette.

The album received significant critical recognition upon its release, being named Rough Trade's album of the week. This achievement is particularly noteworthy given the album's unusual backstory—Campbell had recorded the material four years prior, but legal complications and label closure delayed its release, making the eventual 2020 debut a vindication of her artistic vision.
